questions.answer: An equation is homogeneous when both sides and every term joined by addition or subtraction reduce to the same SI base-unit form. Passing the check shows only that the units are consistent; it does not prove that the physical equation is correct.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent wording that states equality of complete units for all terms and the limited conclusion of a successful check
questions.unit_policy: The answer must refer to SI base-unit forms or equivalent dimensions.
questions.tolerance: Both the condition and the limited conclusion are required for full marks.

marking_points.text: States that both sides and every additive or subtractive term must reduce to the same SI base-unit form
States that passing a homogeneity check does not prove that the physical equation is correct

option_feedback.A: A signed zero reading should be subtracted, and that addresses systematic zero error rather than random variation.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Independent repeated readings expose scatter and their mean allows upward and downward variations to partly cancel.
option_feedback.C: Changing the written unit does not change the variation in the measurement.
option_feedback.D: Reusing one value supplies no independent information and cannot reduce random variation.

questions.answer: Use a micrometer screw gauge. Close it gently with no wire present and observe whether it reads zero. A non-zero value is a zero error that shifts all uncorrected readings consistently. Take corrected readings at several positions and in different orientations around the wire, then calculate their mean.
accepted_alternatives: Suitable digital micrometer or suitably sensitive digital calipers for the instrument, with an equivalent zero check and repeat-and-mean procedure
questions.unit_policy: No numerical unit is required because the task asks for a procedure.
questions.tolerance: Any equivalent physically sound procedure is accepted.

parts.label: (a)
accepted_alternatives: Suitable digital calipers with sufficient sensitivity for the wire

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Close the micrometer gently with no wire between its faces and check whether it reads zero. A non-zero reading is a zero error that adds the same signed offset to every uncorrected diameter reading.
accepted_alternatives: Check the reading when the measuring faces meet, followed by an explanation that the fault biases all readings consistently in the same direction
parts.tolerance: The zero-input condition and consistent effect are both required.

parts.answer: Take readings at several positions along the wire and for different diameter orientations at each position. Apply any zero correction, then calculate the mean of the corrected readings.
accepted_alternatives: A repeat-and-average procedure that samples both lengthwise position and orientation around the wire
parts.tolerance: Both representative sampling and calculation of a mean are required.

questions.answer: The +0.06 g empty reading is a positive zero error and therefore a systematic error because it shifts every sample reading upward. The mean indicated reading is 18.448 g, which is 18.45 g to the display scale. The corrected mean is 18.448 g - 0.06 g = 18.388 g, reported as 18.39 g. Averaging reduces reading-to-reading random variation but keeps the shared +0.06 g offset, so the signed correction is still required.
accepted_alternatives: Correcting each reading by 0.06 g before averaging gives the same corrected mean of 18.388 g
questions.unit_policy: All numerical mass results must include g.
questions.tolerance: Accept 18.448 g or 18.45 g for the indicated mean and 18.388 g or 18.39 g for the corrected mean.

questions.answer: The right-hand unit is [L/t] = m/s = m s^-1, matching [R], so the supplied model is homogeneous. The mean indicated time is 0.204 s and the corrected mean is 0.204 s - 0.004 s = 0.200 s. Averaging addresses the unpredictable scatter among repeated times; subtracting the positive zero reading removes the consistent systematic offset.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent unit notation and correcting each of the five times before taking the same 0.200 s mean
questions.unit_policy: Unit comparisons must use m and s; time results must include s.
questions.tolerance: Exact unit powers and time values to the shown decimal place are required.
